transcript.answer: The web UI uses one WebSocket per browser tab, served by lore-api at `/api/ws` (ADR-048, PR #2122, 2026-09-23). It replaced the earlier run-page SSE stream from ADR-037. The socket carries JSON text frames that multiplex named channels with client-chosen ids. A `run` channel forwards an assembly run's pod events and transcript. It uses a token minted by POST /api/assembly-runs/{id}/stream-token. A `plan` channel tunnels the plan editor's Hocuspocus collaboration bytes to the same collab server, and the collab-token handshake stays inside the tunnel. The web-ui keeps the socket in a provider above every page, so going from a plan to its run keeps the connection. The browser connects directly to lore-api's public host, at `LORE_WS_URL` (`wss://<host>/api/ws`). On the server, one feed per run subscribes once to the Postgres NOTIFY fan-out. The run stream's contract and cursor semantics are unchanged from ADR-037. The SSE route, the web-ui proxy and the EventSource hook were deleted.

judgements.reason: The answer covers one WebSocket per tab at lore-api's /api/ws, JSON frames multiplexing named channels (run, plan), and replacing the per-run SSE stream; omitting the 'runs' channel is minor and contradicts nothing.
